reviewSample.text: I visited Mozart’s Coffee Roasters during the afternoon and enjoyed the relaxed setting by the water. I ordered a coffee and a pastry, and both were good without being overly fancy. The outdoor seating was the best part because it offered a pleasant view of Lake Austin. It was fairly busy, so finding a table took a little time, and the ordering area felt crowded. The staff were polite, and my order came out reasonably quickly. Overall, it was a comfortable place to sit, talk, and enjoy a drink for a while.

My favorite coffee spot in Austin, and I’m sure it’s a favorite for many others too. This place serves amazing coffee along with delicious desserts. They’ve even started serving Indian samosas now, which was such a nice surprise.

The views here are beautiful, and the overall vibe is so relaxing. They also host some really fun events, so definitely check out their events calendar before visiting. Highly recommend this spot if you’re in Austin.

I am in LOVE with Mozart's Coffee Roasters! They are hands-down one of my favorite spots in Austin! The staff is always friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere is perfect for studying, working, or catching up with someone over coffee. It's my go-to choice whenever I'm meeting someone for a coffee date :-)
One of the best parts is the beautiful view of the lake. It's so peaceful, relaxing, and makes spending time there soooo enjoyable. The coffee is also consistently amazing! My favorite drink is the Lavender Latte with either vanilla or honey; absolutely delicious! They also have a few gluten free treats which is great for my gluten allergy

The hasbrowns were a good amount over toasted, dry, and cooked but still definitely manageable when paired with the bacon and eggs. With that being said I would continue to come back so as long as their prices remain this competitive!

If you want a taste of "Real Austin," this is the place to go on Anderson Lane. While this neighborhood has seen a lot of change recently, Russell’s remains a constant. It’s one of the few spots that still feels like the unpretentious, community-focused city I know and love.
The atmosphere is perfect—bright and welcoming but still quiet enough to actually have a conversation or knock out some work. It’s a North Austin staple for a reason.
The Standouts:
The Pastries: Their croissants and cinnamon rolls are easily some of the best in the 78757/78758 area. You can tell they don't cut corners on the butter.
Local Roots: I love that they still serve Anderson Coffee. It’s a great "Austin-on-Austin" partnership that keeps the quality high.
The Vibe: It’s a rare mix of families, professionals, and students. It feels like a neighborhood hub rather than just another sterile coffee chain.
Highly recommend stopping in if you’re anywhere near North Shoal Creek or Wooten. It’s a classic for a reason!
Quick tip for your visit: If they have the Mexican Vanilla cake or cupcakes available when you go, don't skip them. It’s basically an Austin rite of passage.
Enjoy your day off! Are you planning on sticking around Anderson Lane for lunch, or just grabbing a quick caffeine fix?

reviewSample.text:
Oh no—we tragically ran out of coffee beans for our espresso machine! Since coffee is one of my favorite morning rituals, it gave us the perfect excuse to support another incredible local Austin roaster.

We chose Figure 8 Coffee Purveyors, and I was genuinely impressed by the quality, flavor, tasting notes, and variety of beans they offer. The barista was incredibly kind and patient, helping me decide which beans would be the best fit for us. We ultimately brought home three bags: Guatemala, Super Group, and Brazil, and I can’t wait to enjoy each one over the coming weeks.

But amazing coffee isn’t the only thing Figure 8 excels at. I’ve now visited two of their locations, and both experiences were consistently welcoming. Every interaction was filled with kindness and genuine conversation, making each visit feel comfortable and unhurried. The cafés themselves are beautifully designed with a simple, calming aesthetic—perfect for settling in with a laptop for an afternoon of work or simply slowing down to enjoy a great cup of coffee.

Parking has also been refreshingly easy at both locations. Free street parking is available in the surrounding neighborhoods, and the Airport Boulevard location also has its own dedicated parking lot, making it especially convenient to stop in whether you’re grabbing beans to take home or staying awhile.

Karina ordered a lavender latte, while I stuck with my usual oat milk latte, adding just a tiny splash of one of their house-made syrups. I can’t remember the exact name, but it featured rose along with another floral note, and it was absolutely delicious—subtle, unique, and not overly sweet.

Knowing that Figure 8 roasts their coffee in-house under the direction of their talented female roaster makes supporting this local business even more meaningful. If you’re looking for exceptional coffee beans, thoughtfully crafted drinks, genuinely kind people, and a welcoming atmosphere, Figure 8 is absolutely worth a visit.

My favorite coffee shop in Austin ❤️. You can smell the wonderful aroma of coffee roasting as you enter. The baristas are warm, friendly and know how to make great tasting coffee. There’s plenty of seating. Come here for a great start to your day.

☕️ 1 Bean : Austin Espresso at Its Finest
A beautifully dialed-in espresso with outstanding balance. Notes of whiskey, black pepper, and lightly roasted almonds come together in a silky, sweet, and remarkably clean shot. One of the best espresso experiences we have had in Austin. Excellent work from the team at Figure 8 Chicon Street.

reviewSample.text: Great spot on South Congress! I got a cortado and my wife had the house blend, and both were really good. The atmosphere was even better with live music playing and people dancing, which made the place feel very lively and welcoming. Perfect place to grab coffee, relax, and enjoy the Austin vibe.

Jo's Coffee is famous for its iconic "I Love You So Much" mural, which has become one of Austin's most photographed landmarks. Because of all the hype, I was excited to stop by and try the drinks for myself.

Unfortunately, the beverages did not quite live up to my expectations. I tried the coffee, lemonade, and chai latte, and all of them tasted fairly average. Nothing stood out as particularly memorable, and some drinks even felt a little bland.

The one exception was the Turbo. It was by far my favorite item on the menu and the only drink I would strongly recommend. It has a sweet, creamy flavor that reminded me somewhat of an iced Milo, making it much more enjoyable than the other beverages I sampled.

In my opinion, the biggest attraction here is not the coffee but the atmosphere and the photo opportunities. The famous mural makes this a great Instagram spot and a fun place to stop while exploring Austin.

Overall, Jo's Coffee is worth visiting once for the iconic mural and to try the Turbo, but if you're looking for exceptional coffee, you may find the experience a bit overratted.

I've been wanting to check this place out since it's close to my home, and I finally had the perfect opportunity. So I walk in, and it seems like a pretty cool vibe, not too heavy on the hippie vibe, but closer to the stoner. So I scan the menu, which is very small, it's like trying to read one of the eye doctor tests. A little lighting on the board would have helped, so it took a lot longer to find what piqued my curiosity. So I decided to be basic and got a spiced brown sugar frap. So im waiting to place this order I stand at the counter almost 5 minutes watching all the staff look me directly in the eye and never acknowledging im standing here no well be with you in one second no nothing they carry on the conversation amongst each other then finally I guess they got tired of playing whose going to wait on the ghost game and finally one of them broke from what seems to be routine and addressed my order. So my gf and I ordered our coffees and tacos.
The girl pauses in the middle of the order and walks over to grab breakfast tacos from the cooler. I was kinda annoyed that you have a kitchen, but I'm getting these pre-made gas-station breakfast tacos that I assume are batch-cooked weekly and tossed in the fridge with zero effort. The products aren't even dated, so we don't know the proper rotation. So we get our stuff after a few minutes, the food is still cold, we won't complain, and we head home. Once we get home, we reheat the food in the microwave, and you can smell the stink, like it's spoiled. I'm like, ok, maybe it's the gamey smell of the sausage, and I take a bite, and it smells and tastes so bad. These tacos were definitely spoiled, old, and very dry. Like, really, you all need to get your stuff together. As a business owner, I would never take pride in any of this. Like, when did we become so lazy? If you can't do the product right, then why offer it?

Good food, quality coffee, friendly people, and a comfortable atmosphere. Monkey Nest is one of those places that just feels very Austin. An Austin treasure and an easy five stars from me.

The atmosphere is stylish and relaxed, making it a great spot to hang out, work, or unwind. Only issue was the amount of pride flags, but overall, its an easy place to come back to.

reviewSample.text:
We tried Sweet Paris Crêperie & Cafe at The Domain area and really enjoyed it. I ordered the Dulce de Leche crepe and the Dubai Chocolate crepe, and both were amazing in their own way.

The Dulce de Leche was rich, sweet, and very satisfying, while the Dubai Chocolate crepe felt more special and different. Both looked good and tasted even better.

The place itself has a really nice ambience — clean, pretty, and a good spot to sit and enjoy dessert without feeling rushed. The servers were also very friendly and made the experience even better.

Overall, this is a great place if you like crepes, desserts, or just want a nice cafe stop. I’ll definitely come back to try more from the menu.

# Austin Texas

I stopped by Sweet Paris Crêperie & Café for the first time and had a great experience. The restaurant is bright, clean, and beautifully decorated. From the greenery wall outside to the elegant lighting inside, it has a welcoming atmosphere that’s perfect for breakfast, brunch, or just relaxing with a coffee.

I ordered the Iced Strawberry Matcha Latte, and it was outstanding. The matcha was smooth and flavorful, and the fresh strawberry added just the right amount of sweetness without overpowering the drink. It was as good as it looked.

I also appreciated how extensive the menu is. They offer a great selection of sweet and savory crêpes, waffles, croffles, breakfast dishes, coffee, and specialty drinks, so there’s something for everyone.

The staff was friendly, the restaurant was spotless, and everything felt well organized. I’ll definitely be back to try one of their savory crêpes next time. Highly recommend!

Reminds me of Vegas
Really like the vibe, site in probably the most posh area of the Domain.  They do a great job with the atmosphere and the crepes are fantastic.  A generous portion with great flavor.  It's nice when a restaurant gets both of these elements together.
One nit, the matcha wasn't to my liking, they made it too hot and watered down.  It was ok

reviewSample.text: We arrived 20 mins before the store closed. However the staff was very accommodating, attentive and helpful. She helped us with scanning the we code for parking and then scanning their parking validation which was good for 90 mins of free parking. The store offers very open and spacious seating inside. Very good vibes for a date, study, and just hanging out with friends. We ordered an iced latte,  nitro heirloom coffee and lamination cake. Both coffee were amazing. The nitro heirloom was exceptional good and highly recommended. The laminating could be better done. Overall this place is great and worthy for revisits.

This is my new favorite brunch spot in Austin hands down! It was so good we went back 2 times in a week. The scrambled egg with roti, potato hash, and the breakfast burger were all 10/10. Also, you HAVE to ask for the house-made ketchup!!!! It took me by surprise because i wasn’t expecting much, but i was so close to asking if they sell it! A must if you like ketchup with your brunch. The flavors are unique and creative while still being absolutely delicious. The coffee is amazing too. The aussie iced coffee comes with ice cream and once you mix it in it’s the perfect amount of sweetness. Cappuccino is also a 10/10. They usually sell out of their baked goods by the late afternoon, but we got the carrot cake with this amazing cream cheese icing and it was not too sweet and hit the spot after having all the savory food. Parking is very easy, they have a parking lot right outside or you can get your parking validated for the parking garage right next to it, which is always pretty empty. I’m recommending Proud Mary’s to everyone i know, it’s that good! Highly recommend!

My gluten free daughter got gluten free toast, scrambled eggs, and bacon; made a delicious sandwich! My husband got poached eggs on toast that was cooked to Perfection! I had the Best English muffin eggs, cheese, and sausage I’ve ever had; thank you very much! Our lattes were yummy without any bitter tastes; thanks again!
100% Recommend!

Cosmic Coffee at Saltillo Station absolutely blew me away. The place is massive, filled with greenery, and has countless spots to sit, relax, work, or hang out with friends. Every corner feels thoughtfully designed, making it easy to spend hours here.

Everything about this place impressed me—from the atmosphere and layout to the overall energy. It feels like one of those uniquely Austin spots that you immediately want to show your friends.

I can’t wait to come back.

One of my favorite “group” coffee spots in Austin! If you have a big group of friends that you want to meet up with for drinks but have Austin outdoor vibes, Cosmic on Saltillo is definitely one of the best places!

This place is great for a morning coffee or a hair of the dog after a late night!

reviewSample.text: What a delightful coffee shop!  Tasty drip!  I suggest the dark roast.  And, an old-school throw back, $1 refills.  Help yourself!  Loving that trust and vibe.  The facility is enormous for an Austin coffee shop and includes an outdoor patio.  Tables and chairs are mid-century modern art pieces.  Walls are adorned by genuine art, not posters.  Importantly, and hard to find in Austin: not one protest sign, "flag", or banner.  Everybody is welcome at Flight Path!  Also, unlike many Austin joints, the management is serious about not allowing dogs inside the cafe per the health code.  TY!  (Dogs OK on the patio.)  Just a relaxing, welcoming atmosphere in which to enjoy good coffee and snacks. I'd give one million stars if possible.  You won't go wrong by choosing Flightpath.

No frills. Just the basics. ¡Vivan los 90s! The last true second wave coffee shop in Texas. A place where you can spend all day in a coffee shop without going bankrupt. It’s cozy, has cheap refills, and comfortable seating with tons of outlets.

This is a great place to chill out and enjoy a good cold brew. Although we got our customary cappuccino and latte, the barista insisted we try their cold brew as well. Wow. Very buttery smooth! The atmosphere has some hard wood floors, 1960s tables, and enough art on the wall to qualify as a Jackson Pollock exhibit. The coffee was smooth and (wow) served in a real glass glass! It was very flavorful and the barista was super friendly. Plenty of seating inside. If there was a negative, it would be not a lot of parking. Thankfully you can park in the street nearby.

reviewSample.text:
We went to Two Hands for brunch on a Sunday.  It was busy, but not overcrowded, and we had a reservation!

We started with Crispy Brussels Spouts and they were defininitely a favorite and so delicious!  The tables on either side of us ordered the Brussels as well!

I had the Two Hander Burger and it was great.  Very good Montana Waygu beef!  It comes with shoestring style french fries that reminded me of my childhood and were so crisp and tasty (see picture!). We also had the Salmon Quinoa Bowl which is a tasty, healthy choice, salmon was terrific.
The Steak and Egg was quality.  The steak was slightly underseasoned but the French anchovy dressing more than made up for it!  The hashbrowns and egg were both great with it!  Lastly, we had the Smashed Avo Toast with smoked Salmon and it was wonderful.
Also recommend the Hot Vanilla Orange Blossom Latte and for dessert, the Banana Walnut Bread topped with Espresso Mascarpone, so decadent!

The atmosphere and the service was amazing! However, the food doesn’t reflect the price listed and the water tastes off. Otherwise no complaints on the food as the flavors were on point, would recommend to anyone trying this place out for the first time.

Love the vibe and the food is good.

The fritters were good (I’ve had better but it was good!). The viet rice bowl was really good!!! I’d recommend getting extra rice bc just the mushroom was overwhelming the served rice portion + more pepper too.

The staff is super nice and attentive and the extra rice wasn’t an added charge.

reviewSample.text:
This place was the perfect experience. As the city grows, it escapes the original energy that used to exist on the east side. This helped bring it back to me. The people, the music, & especially the smoothies & treats.

I had a savory danish which B, the friendly person working the window offered to warm up. I had the golden kiss shot which was very delicious, I sipped on it more than anything because I didn’t want it to finish.

My smoothie was the (I Know) which had lavender pellets on top which was yummy. I also got to sample a delicious blue smoothie that tasted like a light coconut breeze if that makes sense.

Overall this place helped me disconnect and reconnect with how I used to feel roaming the east side for zen spots back in the day.

This place is the cutest smoothie shop.
I recently visited Austin and was so happy I discovered this place next to my air bnb.

I’m in love with all the vibes here, the drinks and the aesthetics. I especially loved the names of all the drinks and the combinations.

I wish we had one of these back in Cali. Shout out to Bee who sent me home with a souvenir. A 369 manifestation journal. Absolutely nice to have a delicious smoothie to cleanse me, but with manifestations a delightful surprise. Can’t wait to come back and visit this again.

TLDR: long wait, mishandled order, rude service, and an $11 juice that was wildly unbalanced.

I visited on 3/18/26 around 2:30 PM with a friend. The space felt calm and inviting, and parking was easy — which made the experience that followed even more disappointing. There was one man working, and I understand being short-staffed, so we were patient. After waiting well over 20 minutes for our drinks, I was told at the window that my falafel bowl had never been processed and hadn't even been started. When I asked politely how much longer it would take, he said 10–15 minutes. I thanked him, said I'd come back another time, and even told him I appreciated him. He rolled his eyes and shut the window in my face. Maybe it was a hard day — but that level of hostility was completely unnecessary toward a patient, polite customer. I'm more than happy to spend my money elsewhere.

The concept and menu still have potential

One of my favorite hidden gems in Austin for remote working or just enjoying a delicious coffee. Staff is always so friendly and accommodating and their drink are superb. The 16oz Coldbrew with honey syrup hit the spot! Lake was also super helpful in giving me a quick rundown on skateboard shopping.

atmosphere in the cafe was nice, found it cool that it was connected to a skate shop. didn’t know what i wanted, barista named vy guided me through the menu. i got the vanilla cappuccino and it was really good.

I had to ask her if it was my coffee, and she just nodded. However, she did call out the order of other customers. I wish coffee shops would stop asking for tips while doing the bare minimum :/

This is one of my favorite coffee shops in town, especially because it stays open until 7 p.m. on Sundays—something that’s surprisingly hard to find! I couldn’t come visit ATX with my pup and not check out Dog Day Coffee.
So, we came here on a chill Sunday morning, I enjoyed a latte with oat milk which I found a little too mild and she got a whipped cream treat.
The atmosphere was nice, just like the service.
So yeah not the most spectacular coffee, but a good pace to hang out in. Cheers.

When we came to Austin for a long weekend from Denver, I was blown away with the quality of their nitro and loved the atmosphere. The staff were so friendly and I’m still over here daydreaming about the next time I can get some dog day coffee. We tried the Imperial and the house and really enjoyed both, but have to say the house was a favorite. Can’t rave about this place enough. Thank you Dog Day. 🫶🏻

Lovely quiet coffee spot with an industrial aesthetic. Plenty of outlets to plug in your computer. Also has some gluten free pastry options I have not tried. Typically order a dairy free matcha. drink.name: White Vanilla Miso Matcha Latte
drink.reason: The white vanilla miso flavor (as a latte or matcha latte) is the most praised signature drink, mentioned across multiple 5-star reviews for its silky, smooth, balanced umami-sweet profile.
drink.quote: silky-milky with a hint of umami giving a nice brightness

reviewSample.text:
Desnudo absolutely lived up to the hype. We tried the Brown Sugar Miso Latte, the White Vanilla Miso Latte, and the White Miso Matcha, and every single drink was incredible. The flavors were unique without being overpowering—smooth, perfectly balanced, and unlike anything we’ve had at another coffee shop. The matcha was especially memorable!

We also shared the chocolate croissant, which was fresh, buttery, and flaky—the perfect pairing with the drinks.

The service was just as impressive as the coffee. Everyone was welcoming, happy to answer questions, and genuinely excited about what they were serving. The outdoor patio is such a relaxing place to sit and enjoy your coffee.

If you’re in Austin and appreciate thoughtfully crafted coffee, Desnudo is a must-visit. We left already talking about what we want to try the next time we’re in town.

This was my first time visiting Desnudo and I can definitely see why people love it.

I wasn’t sure what to order so I asked for a recommendation. The sweet lady at the front suggested the Guava Matcha and since I wanted something refreshing, it ended up being exactly what I was looking for. I tasted the matcha but also the guava and was a great combination. For me one of the best matcha drinks I’ve had in a while.

The space is cute, with outdoor seating if you want to hang out for a bit (they play really good music). Service was quick and I also loved that they sell bags of coffee to take home. There’s even a lovely plant shop right across the way, which makes the whole area feel even more nice.The only thing to keep in mind is that parking can be a bit of a hassle, so be prepared for that.

This feels like one of those coffee spots you can keep coming back to whenever you’re craving coffee or matcha. I’ll definitely be back!

Great to meet you again, team! Amazing signature menu as always. I thoroughly enjoyed both the white vanilla miso and the shoyu butterscotch. The white vanilla miso was silky-milky with a hint of umami giving a nice brightness to the creamy body. The shoyu butterscotch was a lovely interplay between caramel and umami, albeit a brighter showcase of the caramel velvety texture with the umami supporting the aftertaste. The shoyu butterscotch is, in a way, a brighter and more caramel-forward presentation of the same idea carried by the brown sugar miso.
It took me a while to finally visit y'all down at this new location since it was opened up. There is a patio area in front and an indoor air-conditioned area attached to Frond Plant Shop next door accessible through a little gate entrance. The light birch furniture interlaced with green accents from purchasable plants from the Plant Shop is a lovely touch, and along with a cool indie pop playlist and great (as always) signature syrups and garnishes that pair lovely with the house blend, it showcases well how the partnership creates for a cute relaxing atmosphere you both have cultivated.

Thank you again for having me y'all, and as always don't be strangers :)

reviewSample.text: Absolutely in love with this coffee shop!  I wish there was one just like it where I live.  My love and I were traveling through to Corpus and decided to skip coffee at the hotel and grab something at a local coffee shop, since we love supporting local shops when we travel.  When we walked in, I felt like I was transported to a friendly apothecary in a fantasy novel (and I'm positive my cousin Miranda Lyn would love this place).  The atmosphere and decor is fun, decorative, yet mellow and relaxing, with a perfect touch of seasonal decor for December.  The chandeliers are incredible and really add to the magic. The place is small, yet has plenty of seating inside and out. The music was at a comfortable level with an awesome mix of contemporary and classic rock.   There were books and games available on shelves.   The owners were the ones working and they were super kind and helpful.  The coffees we got were really good and the coffee was strong, yet smooth and not bitter at all...much like you would expect lovely merfolk to be ;).

Whimsical, magical, fantastical, and simply fantastic themed coffee shop in South Austin. The coffee was delicious, the aesthetic was colorful, and the workers on staff were awesome. Definitely a great spot to enjoy coffee, read, work remotely, and meet up with your friends.

I wanted to swing by Merfolk on my way to work and ended up arriving a bit before their official open time of 7:30, but the doors were open at 7:25 so it was nice I didn't have to wait! Taylor was very friendly (especially for the early hour lol) and greeted me promptly when I walked in.  I wasn't sure what to order off the special menu and Taylor took the time to explain the concept to me and give his suggestion (the maple one which was delicious!). I was a little hesitant as all of the specialty drinks seemed to have a ton of syrup in them and I like my coffee less sweet, but he said it was no problem to make any of the drinks half-sweet which I did.

I liked that they were down to use my coffee tumbler that I brought with me, and the coffee was out super fast.  The maple latte was delicious and fit the cooler weather perfectly!  The theme and decor of the shop is a lot of fun, and I particularly enjoyed the big mural on the front wall (the dragon bats are the best!).  I'm looking forward to coming back and trying more coffees!

Visited Bakery Lorraine at The Domain Northside and really liked the overall experience. The vibe is warm and inviting, and the staff is friendly and helpful, which makes it a pleasant place to spend time.

I tried their hot chocolate, and it was good — I’d rate it around 3.5/5. It wasn’t outstanding, but still enjoyable. What really stands out is the atmosphere. It’s a great spot to sit, relax, and even get some work done for a few hours.

If you’re in The Domain and looking for a comfortable café with a nice ambience, this is a solid choice.

My favorite place in the Domain! Fast-casual counter-ordering service that brings fresh food to your table. Great for meeting with family or friends, or for working solo thanks to the coveted ledge seating with a perfect window view of the Rock Rose street walkers. There’s also plenty of indoor and outdoor covered seating. Their coffee is fantastic with tons of options, they offer wine & glass-bottled sodas, a variety of delectable pastries, and a seasonal menu full of fresh, real food.

My only hope is that you’re here while they’re serving either the Turkish eggs or the Cuban sandwich — both go absolutely crazy. I love to travel, but I often find it overwhelming to eat out constantly, especially when the only available options are heavy or fried foods. Sometimes you just want something light, fresh, and healthy to feel better.

I found a perfect spot that offers exactly that. The moment you walk in, the lighting, plants, and overall ambiance create a refreshing atmosphere. There is even an outdoor seating area that provides a quiet escape from the overstimulation of the mall—it's a great place to disconnect and recalibrate.

I’ve attached photos of the menu and my order, which included a toast, a bowl, and a smoothie. The plant displays really add to the experience and help you feel grounded. I highly recommend checking it out if you're looking for a fresh, healthy meal.

The avocado smash, smoked salmon and açaí bowls were absolutely delicious. The coffee was one of the best ones that I’ve had in Austin. Everything was very fresh. The staff was very friendly and the food came out quickly. 10/10. We’ll definitely be coming back!

reviewSample.text:
Klerje Coffee has such a unique and elegant vibe! This coffee shop is decorated beautifully. The staff are INCREDIBLY sweet! I noticed that they seem to have a lot of regular customers, which is always a good sign! Although I wasn’t a big fan of what I ordered, I’m still eager to come back to try other items from their menu. Bravo to the staff and founders for creating a lovely atmosphere and coffee shop!

^^ I will say that the shop has limited seating, so if you’re a college student like me, try coming as early as possible to secure a table!

Fantastic specialty coffee shop in East Austin. They carry Black & White and Makeworth and Metric. Their pourovers are very nice, I am guessing it's a 3-pour based on the fruit balance. The space is also very friendly to work and to converse. For the mornings, it's definitely an array of laptops on the weekdays but I can see on the weekends or on Fridays this being a place to catch up about the week's goings. The owners are also very knowledgeable about coffee and the coffee world so if you need help follow them.

Also congratulations on the marriage!

Specialty coffee bar with top-notch coffee & FANTASTIC customer service.

Went to Klerje multiple times during our visit to Austin and the experience was consistent.

Staff behind the bar is super friendly and helpful, you know that they love their job and it’s not like some places where you feel like you just have to hurry up and order and get out of the way.

Other patrons are also friendly and happy to chat as well, like there’s this sense of community in there that you just don’t find everywhere, people striking up conversations, regulars saying hi to the staff by name, that whole thing.

Overall, this is the kind of coffee shop that every community needs. If you’re visiting Austin from out of town, make sure you go check them out, you will not regret it.

With love from from deep South Texas, Jeremy

My husband and I were looking for a place to hang that had free Wifi and this place totally hits the spot. We were impressed with the coffee drinks as usually super aesthetic places sometimes don't make the best coffee hoping how cute the cafe is will make you pay less attention to the drinks, but here we can tell care and quality are put into each drink. Parking is free and easy with a large lot attached

I ordered the Jelly Donut Focaccia, and it was absolutely delicious. I had never even heard of a sweet focaccia before, so it was a must try, and it definitely didn’t disappoint.

I paired it with the white ginger pear tea, and together they made the perfect combo for this gloomy and rainy day.

Shoutout to Tony, the owner, for creating such a cool spot. I’ll be back!

I am such a big fan of this place! The atmosphere, the decor, the coffee, the treats, I love it all. I live next door and walk here often and sometimes work from here. The music is always a vibe in here and makes it a relaxing environment. They always have new and fun sweet treats that are always absolutely delicious. The blueberry scone is OUT OF THIS WORLD DELICIOUS!

Outdoor area with astroturf lets you enjoy the weather and order fresh and delicious tacos from the Mexican food truck. There are breakfast tacos available and some pastries too. There’re enough tables to sit and work without feeling cramped - the wifi is stable as well. We grabbed an iced coffee and tea, then found a quiet spot on the terrace to relax. The outdoor seating is shaded and peaceful, perfect for catching up with friends or just people-watching with a cool drink in hand. Indoors, the decor feels like a cross between a boutique lounge and an artist’s studio refined but not fussy.

If you’re looking for a chill place to start your day or wind down in the evening, Simona’s is the spot. They serve both craft cocktails and specialty coffee, so whether you’re a latte lover or a cocktail enthusiast, you’ll feel right at home.

Don’t forget to explore the hotel’s art-filled lobby and take a few shots around the terrace the natural light is perfect for photos!

reviewSample.text: I visited the café today, for the first time, with a friend who's been many times and has raved about it. The food was so delicious! I had the vegetable quiche, pain au chocolat, and a honey lavender latte. I really liked the atmosphere as well. The cafe is very airy with lots of natural light. French music was playing and that, combined with the wonderful food, made it feel like a little trip to France in the heart of Austin.

Came skeptical. “Parisian-style café” usually means a sad croissant with the integrity of a dinner roll. Wrong. The lamination’s the real thing — that buttery shatter that ruins your coat and you forgive instantly. The jambon-beurre on the le Parisien is the sandwich I’ve been quietly mourning for years: good ham, good butter, good bread, rien d’autre.

And it shape-shifts. Mornings, espresso and people pretending to read. Evenings, champagne and Aperol spritzes under the string lights, the picnic tables suddenly feeling like a sidewalk on the Rue de Buci. All for ten to twenty bucks — which, after a decade of paying fourteen for a worse latte, still feels like getting away with something.

Is it Paris? No. The sky’s too big, the light too generous. But that’s the charm.

Go early for the pastries. Stay late for the wine.

With a name that translates to big/lots of love, Grá Mór, an offshoot of The Dead Rabbit, seems to be tempting fate. Admittedly, an Irish café in a historical building oozes charm. We came in search of breakfast and split an order of Scotch eggs and a Full Irish, to which we added a Banana Cream Cold Brew and a Blueberry Crumble Latte. The eggs featured crumbly sausage and a crispy coating while the Full Irish boasted a copious amount of food: eggs, bacon, sausage, black and white pudding, grilled tomato, baked beans, potato bread, and butter. reviewSample.text:
Another La La Land location! It’s funny seeing people complain about the parking at this location - at least they have 10 dedicated spots for parking compared to the SoCo location which has zero parking spots dedicated to the store. I will say their parking lot is one way only (enter off 45th street) and the signage needs to be better at the exit saying “do not enter” as I saw tons of car going the wrong way and having to reverse out. I will be curious how their drive thru will work once it is up and running. There is also street parking nearby if you’re  willing to walk 3 minutes. I found parking on Rosedale near the park and only took me 3 minutes to walk with a stroller. There was also free parking located near Rosedale Baptist church.

Located on the corner of Burnet and 45th, I came here on their soft opening week when drinks were 50% off (currently still going on until tomorrow 6/20/26). I have always loved Là Là Land matcha drinks - I got their strawberry matcha and banana cloud matcha. Both were deliciously good without being overpoweringly sweet. Indoor seating wise they only have about 5-6 tables of 2 and outside they do have a patio. We went on a cloudy day and sat on the patio, but likely won’t recommend it on a super sunny day as there wasn’t much umbrella coverage at all.

Overall a great LaLaLand location that is located more central than their SoCo one, but I do like the SoCo one better for interior wise as it is a larger store.

I really can’t wait for the Domain location to open. I think that will be the best LaLaLand combo - easy free Domain garage parking and large store footprint.

Hearing about the soft opening me and my friends were super excited to try. There’s only about 10 parking spaces which we had to parked down the street not horrible. They also closed drive thru due to too much traffic. The line moved relatively fast and ordering was simple and sweet. After that moment the vibes changed. People started reserving spots while still waiting in line which evidently took up all the indoor space leaving us to have to wait for a good covered spot outside. I say good covered because the coverage outside is horrible and that’s where the most seating is at. Our drinks came out fast, but they were very behind on toasts. They offered one of my friends the hazelnut toast while the other one they did not because they were out due to a shortage of strawberries that just arrived. With that we had to wait 20 mins for that toast. All of our other drinks and toast came out within 10 mins of ordering. It just was a little off when trying to all eat together and super super hot. Hopefully in the future these things will improve.
